title.narrative: EnACT- Enabling Access to Justice, Civil Society Participation and Transparency

description.narrative: This action primarily consists of a contribution agreement with GIZ to carry out activities on legislation formulation and implementation; support to accountbaility mechanisms; and access to justice initatives focused on legal aid. There is a significant crosscutting component on enhancing civil society participation in all the target sectors.The action intends to contribute to MIP priority area 3 to build a more fair, inclusive and peaceful society in Zambia and ensure collaboration between government authorities and non-state actors. Particular focus will be on specific objective (SO) 3.1- Promoting human rights and improve the democratic space for citizens in Zambia under the result related to the promotion of rule of law and respect of human rights. The action also contributes to SO 3.2 - Supporting public sector reform for improved delivery of public services and domestic accountability under the result to improve the efficiency, accountability and transparency of the public administration, enabling quality public service delivery. It contributes to the 2030 Agenda and Sustainable Development Goals (16, 5 and 10), the Addis Ababa Action Agenda, the new European Consensus on Development as well as the EU Action Plan on Human Rights and Democracy, the EU-Zambia CSO Roadmap and the Gender Action Plan III.This action is the first truly joint programme in Zambia. In a ¿Team Europe¿ spirit, it has been designed in close collaboration with, and co-funding from, Germany and with GIZ as implementing partner. The action builds upon successful programmes on access to justice, accountability and civil society participation, funded by the EU under the 11th EDF and Germany. As a result, this action will accommodate both the broad commitment of Germany as well as the EU current support on public sector accountability and transparency, and the more focussed EU engagement on access to justice. The EU is cooperating with other Member States, including Sweden and Ireland, to ensure complementarity and continuously explore opportunities to include other Member States into joint programming in order to increase outreach and impact of this Action. NOTE- In the Timeline section "Ares strategic validation reference" there was no Ares validation for this Action, so I attach the Decision information instead as this information is important to reflect in OPSYS. title.narrative: Number of people who were able to access justice supported by the EU intervention (disaggregated by sex, gender, age, disability, as well as type of support provided)

description.narrative: Under people, this indicator counts clients, cases and complaints, depending on the terminology and reporting mechanism of each institution. In this indicator, access to justice refers to individuals, who have accessed a paralegal or public human rights complaint mechanisms.Specifically, this indicator includes:Complaints received, investigations undertaken, and recommendations given by the Human Rights Commission.Clients of paralegal desks. At community desk level it includes all kinds of legal aid services, At PSD,LSU,CFD level only cases where legal advise by paralegals was given are countedComplaints to OPPZ that were investigated.Complaints to ACC that were investigated.Awareness raising activities are not included in this indicator.Baselines, targets and annual updates should report values for each institution separately to accurately monitor changes in case uptake and investigation as well as people benefitting from paralegal desks.

comment.narrative: Complaints from ACC and OPPZ are unfortunately not disaggregated by sex and age thus we only count them as people and the male and female values dont sum up to the total value.

Complaints from ACC and OPPZ are unfortunately not disaggregated by sex and age thus we only count them as people and the male and female values dont sum up to the total value.We calculated the increase of the target number of OPPZ ACC and HRC with a ten percent increase per year based on the baseline value.We decided to report an accumulative target for the end of 2025. The reason is that we will slowly reduce our support for legal aid interventions in 2025. As the project tries to implement sustainable structures in the legal aid sector it will reduce its amount of funding in 2025 substantially to test how sustainable the provision of legal aid in Zambia is. Therefore the numbers for 2025 wil be a lot lower then for the rest of the years. Thus we only report on an accumulative target.

title.narrative: Increased citizens demand of state accountability mechanisms

description.narrative: Support capacity building trainings of local level CSOs, particularly youth and womens organizations, on their rights as citizens. This includes training on how to hold state institutions accountable, e.g. through monitoring of public service delivery, active engagement in dialogue with duty bearers, public expenditure tracking or by making use of public complaint mechanisms Support CSOs advocacy capacity on the impact of systemic corruption, specifically on groups living in the most vulnerable situations (genderbased corruption, access barriers for people with disabilities, etc.), including citizens awareness and dialogue with state institutions Build capacity of CSOs in documenting and reporting corruption to ensure transparent public service delivery in the social sectors, with a strong focus on education Promote safe spaces for participation of women and girls, youth, and people with disabilities in local and subnational institutions

title.narrative: Number of citizens and members of CSOs trained by the EUfunded intervention with increased knowledge and/or skills on a gender and rightsbased approach to accountability, disaggregated by sex and age

description.narrative: For the activity to count as a training, there must be a structured approach to knowledge transfer (not merely sensitisation). To assess increased knowledge and skills on a gender and rightsbased approach to accountability, an assessment must be conducted before and after the trainings. These can be based on more traditional ways of assessment, such as test or quizzes or involve alternative ways of measuring learning effect in a systematic way.

comment.narrative: Based on participants lists of trainings carried out between August 2021 until January 2023.
Based on past trainings participants lists we anticipate that around 20 percent of the participants are children as part of the trainings are held at schools.

title.narrative: Enhanced capacity of state institutions to formulate laws and policies in a transparent manner

description.narrative: Support government in the participatory and evidencebased formulation/revision of key legislation, such as the AntiCorruption Act, HRC Act, Public Order Act, Juvenile Act/Child Code Bill, Penal Code and Criminal Procedure Code Support dialogue and consultation platforms between Government institutions and civil society organisation on law and policy making, for consultations on the Public Order Act. Build capacity through mentoring and training of civil society organisations and networks to give expert input into the design of legislation that is gender sensitive and respecting the principle of `leave no one behind Build capacity of state actors regarding the inclusion of women, people living with disabilities, young people and other groups living in the most vulnerable situations and to ensure their needs are reflected in law reforms. This may include trainings, advisory services and dialogue.

title.narrative: GERF 2.29 Number of government policies developed or revised with civil society organisation participation through EU support

description.narrative: Policies are understood as described under Outcome 1.Participation can include CSO consultations, engagement, written and oral submissions and other forms of participation. Policy development refers to new policies, which have been submitted to the responsible decisionmaking authority.Policy revision refers to changes to existing policies (this can include reviews or changes in policy approaches).GERF This indicator refers to the number of government policies and strategies developed with Civil Society Organisation (CSO) participation through EU support. The EU considers CSOs to include all nonState, notforprofit structures, nonpartisan and nonviolent, through which people organise to pursue shared objectives and ideals, whether political, cultural, social or economic.

comment.narrative: Accumulative targetSupport to processes on such asNational AntiCorruption Policy developmentRevision and Development of NGO policyRevision of ReEntry policyAmendment of AntiCorruption ActAmendment of Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes ActConstitution reforms including Bill of RightsNLAPRegulations under CSAPC and CPC

Build capacity through mentoring and training of civil society organisations and networks to give expert input into the design of legislation that is gender sensitive and respecting the principle of `leave no one behind Build capacity of state actors regarding the inclusion of women, people living with disabilities, young people and other groups living in the most vulnerable situations and to ensure their needs are reflected in law reforms. This may include trainings, advisory services and dialogue.

title.narrative: GERF 2.29 Number of government policies developed or revised with civil society organisation participation through EU support

description.narrative: Policies are understood as described under Outcome 1.Participation can include CSO consultations, engagement, written and oral submissions and other forms of participation. Policy development refers to new policies, which have been submitted to the responsible decisionmaking authority.Policy revision refers to changes to existing policies (this can include reviews or changes in policy approaches).GERF This indicator refers to the number of government policies and strategies developed with Civil Society Organisation (CSO) participation through EU support. The EU considers CSOs to include all nonState, notforprofit structures, nonpartisan and nonviolent, through which people organise to pursue shared objectives and ideals, whether political, cultural, social or economic.

description.narrative: Mechanisms can include formal or informal established processes to implement policies in a transparent and inclusive manner. Formal` means written rules, shared expectations, and norms that are enshrined in formally constituted organizations and documents. Involvement means that the mechanisms need to support the participation of CSOs in the policymaking process.Functioning means that it fulfils its intended purpose.

title.narrative: Country Score according to the Bertelsmann Transformation Index (BTI)

description.narrative: The Bertelsmann Transformation Index (BTI) analyses and evaluates the quality of democracy, a market economy and political management in 129 developing and transition countries. It measures successes and setbacks on the path toward a democracy based on the rule of law and a socially responsible market economy. The BTI Status Index ranks countries according to their quality of democracy and market economy as of January 31, 2015.The state of political transformation is measured in terms of five criteria (Stateness, Political participation; Rule of Law; Stability of democratic Institutions; Political and social integration), which in turn are derived from assessments made in response to 18 questions. Political Participation is measured by the normative statement: The populace decides who rules and it has other political freedoms.Thresholds determine five categories:Excellent (8.5010.00); Sound (6.50 8.49); Fair (4.50 6.49); Flawed (2.50 4.49); Poor (1.00 2.49)More detail on the concepts used can be found here https://btiproject.org/en/?&cb00000

comment.narrative: As the Index is only published biannually we took the NDICI Governance index score 2022 of Zambia as a baseline value. As there are only integers allowed we put in 391 instead of 3.91.

There is limited causal attribution of EnACT. Therefore as score of 5.48 is a bestcase scenario and the target should most importantly reflect an improvement compared to 2022. Moreover as the Index is only published biannually we took the NDICI Governance index score 2024 of Zambia as a target value. As there are only integers allowed we put in 548 instead of 5.48.

title.narrative: Number of state and nonstate actors (individuals) trained by the EUfunded intervention with increased knowledge and/or skills on human rights principles and contemporary human rights challenges in regional, national or international context, disaggregated (OPSYS core indicator)

description.narrative: This indicator refers to trainings of state actors and CSOs. Each actor (individual) is to be counted once in the lifetime of an EUfunded intervention, even in cases where the same actor participates in different training sessions.To determine increased knowledge, a form of assessment or evaluation should be carried out before and/or after the trainings. These can be based on more traditional ways of assessment, such as test or quizzes or involve alternative ways of measuring learning effect in a systematic way.We count the following trainings:1. Trainings on human rights principles at local courts of magistrates and clerks2. Trainings on human rights principles of traditional court adjudicators3. Trainings on human rights principles at police stations of officers (Training of Trainers Topics on diversion/ duty to provide information legal laid/ rights of suspects and Police Bond)4. Correctional service trainings at correctional facilities of ZCS Officers (topics New Mandate of ZCS and the duty to provide information on legal aid)5. Paralegal trainings (refresher and some inital trainings in all target provinces) at the LSUs, correctional facility, police station legal desks and community legal desks.
